name: Morse.geodesicIndex
hypotheses: γ ∈ Ω(N; p, q) (Morse.pathSpace N p q); no geodesic hypothesis needed
difference: Junk value outside the textbook domain: for γ ∉ Ω(N; p, q) the project returns 0, while the blind (which ignores p, q) evaluates the index of its E_** at γ anyway (e.g. for a path in Ω(N; p', q') with other endpoints it gives that path's index). Both send an infinite index to 0 via ENat.toNat. Not formalized as a counterexample (it needs a path with positive finite index).
why: For γ ∈ Ω the blind TΩ_γ is the project's pathTangent and the blind E_** is energyHessian transported along that equality (dictionary + secondVariation_eq_hessForm); the blind index (sup over all negative definite subspaces of rank.toENat) equals Morse.formIndex (as for Morse_formIndex), and formIndex is invariant under the isometric linear equivalence (formIndex_le_of_map both ways); then both take toNat.
